question.problem:
Find the $25$th percentile of the random variable $X$ if the probability distribution function of $X$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}-1,\, & 2<x<4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The $100p$th percentile of a random variable $X$ is the number ${x}_{p}$ such that

$$
P(X\le {x}_{p})=p.
$$

In our case, we want to find the $25$th percentile, which corresponds to the decimal $p=0.25.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le {x}_{0.25}) & ={\int }_{2}^{{x}_{0.25}}(\frac{x}{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-x)|}_{2}^{{x}_{0.25}} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{0.25}^{2}}{4}-{x}_{0.25}-(\frac{(2)^{2}}{4}-2) \\  & =\frac{{x}_{0.25}^{2}}{4}-{x}_{0.25}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $25$th percentile is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}_{0.25}^{2}}{4}-{x}_{0.25}+1 & =0.25 \\ {x}_{0.25}^{2}-4{x}_{0.25}+3 & =0 \\ ({x}_{0.25}-3)({x}_{0.25}-1) & =0 \\ {x}_{0.25}=1,\,3.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we take the root ${x}_{0.25}=3$ because $2<{x}_{0.25}<4.$
